ov: Long-haired domesticated cattle of the Himalayas, the Tibetan Plateau and the mountains of Central Asia, north to Mongolia and Siberia, descended from the wild yak. Larger lungs and heart than lowland cattle, dense shaggy fur and a thick layer of fat suit it to high, cold places.

why.dm: Most yaks are domestic; they descend from the wild yak, a separate species.
why.et: Kept for milk, wool and meat, and some farmers' only meat through harsh winters.

rg: The Himalayas, Tibetan Plateau, Pamirs and Tajikistan, north to Mongolia and Siberia.

cf.tip: Yaks are close relatives of cattle and bison, adapted to high altitude.

fx: Yaks don’t moo like cattle; they grunt and squeak, which gave the domestic yak its scientific name, “grunting ox”.
Yaks struggle at lower altitudes, and can suffer heat exhaustion above about 15 °C.
